objective: Stock can be reserved beyond what is free. With 10 units on hand of which 8 are already reserved, reserving 3 more units succeeds and the available stock becomes negative; repeated reservations over-commit the same stock. Only units that are available (on hand minus reserved) may be reserved. A refused request raises a `StockError` and changes nothing.
acceptance: With 10 units received and 6 reserved, reserving 5 raises a `StockError` and leaves 10 on hand, 6 reserved and 4 available
Reservations of 3, 3 and 4 units of a stock of 10 succeed, leaving 0 available, and a further reservation of 1 raises a `StockError`
For levels loaded with 10 on hand and 8 reserved, reserving 3 raises a `StockError`, reserving 2 succeeds (10 on hand, 10 reserved), and a SKU with 5 on hand and 5 reserved cannot be reserved at all

After 10 received, 6 reserved and 2 shipped (8 on hand, 4 reserved), reserving 5 raises a `StockError` and reserving 4 succeeds; after releasing 3, reserving 4 raises a `StockError` and reserving 3 succeeds; after receiving 2 more, reserving 2 succeeds
Reserving an unknown SKU raises a `StockError` and creates no entry; a quantity of 0 or less raises a `StockError` and changes nothing
The low-stock list follows the available stock after reservations (a refused reservation does not change it)

For a seeded random sequence of receive, reserve, release and ship calls, a reserve call succeeds exactly when its quantity is at most the available stock, every refused call leaves the levels unchanged, and the available stock never becomes negative
